perspective.publicDescription: Workers report shift bells and fresh industrial injuries beside the dismantled Eastbank service spur. Mutual aid asks for an independent site record.

runtime.late: Safety barriers are now in place. Request an escort or use worker-held traces; no lost single clue.
runtime.preparation: Arrange worker accompaniment, isolate moving apparatus and mark the exit. After closure this provides escorted inspection permission, not immunity.
runtime.testimony: Emil Hart reports a shift bell where the service rails were removed; workers describe injuries along the old timetable. This is a report, not a demonstrated cause.

sources.text: A timed perimeter recording captures a repeated shift bell and fresh wheel-scoring at the dismantled spur during its obsolete shift interval.
Certified dismantling order and dispatch appendix show coordinated Eastbank movements on a supposedly idle service route during reconstruction.
A witnessed inner-yard inspection records fresh mechanism pressure at the obsolete loading line; the dangerous pattern is repeatable, not an ordinary scheduled train.
Consented worker-held shift stubs match an obsolete spur code across several coordinated evacuation shifts absent from the public route summary.
